transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Um… I guess the main thing is my eating’s been kind of off lately. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but some days before a shift I’m basically just getting down coffee and maybe a granola bar, and that’s about it. And my scrubs have been fitting looser, like hanging on me more, even though I’m not trying to lose weight. I figured I should probably come in and ask about it.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

No, not really. I mean… I’m not trying to lose weight or anything like that. It’s more that my appetite’s been off, I guess. Some mornings before work I can barely get down coffee and maybe a granola bar, and then I notice my scrubs are hanging looser. It’s not because I’m worried about gaining weight, if that makes sense.
When you try to eat before a shift, do you feel anxious?

I’m not sure I’d call it anxious, exactly. I mean, maybe a little tense because I know I need to get to work and I don’t want to feel sick or anything, but I haven’t really noticed it as, like, fear around eating. It’s more just… my stomach doesn’t seem interested, if that makes sense.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to overstate it, because I’m still getting to work and everything. But most mornings I wake up with this kind of heavy, hollow feeling, like the day’s already gone bad before I even put my badge on. I don’t know if that counts as depressed, but… it’s been there.
Did this start after something particularly stressful happened?

I guess… yeah, kind of. It wasn’t one big dramatic thing, but it started after the clinic changed over the EMR and redid the workflow. My hours shifted with all that, and I’ve just sort of been dealing with it since then. It’s been almost two years now, if I’m remembering right.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about different parts of your life, even when there isn’t an immediate problem?

I don’t know… not across everything, I don’t think. I mean, I worry about work stuff and keeping up, normal things like bills or being on time, but I wouldn’t say I’m sitting there worrying about every part of my life for no reason. At least, I haven’t really thought of it that way. Does that make sense?
Have you been enjoying things less than you usually do?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I still try to tell myself I could do things, but I don’t really follow through much anymore. I used to run in Van Cortlandt Park, take photos, play chess with friends… normal stuff I actually liked.

Lately I’ll think about it and then just kind of go, “What’s the point?” and stay home instead. I end up scrolling on my phone or checking my budget spreadsheet, which sounds productive, I guess, but it’s not really enjoyable. I don’t know if that’s the kind of thing you mean.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

Yeah… a bit. I mean, I do sleep, it’s not like I’m up all night every night, but it’s pretty broken up.

I’ll lie there replaying stuff from work, and I’m kind of listening for noises, if that makes sense. Then I’ll wake up around 3 or 4 in the morning and I can’t really settle back down before the alarm. I don’t know if that counts as insomnia exactly, but it’s been happening.
Have you had unwanted memories of a frightening or disturbing event that keep coming back?

Not really, no. I mean… I’ve had upsetting things happen like anyone, but I don’t think I have memories that come back in that way, like I’m reliving something. If I’m understanding what you mean, I don’t think that’s been a big issue for me.
Have you been feeling this way most days for at least two weeks?

Yeah… yes, I think so. More than two weeks, definitely.

I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but the more steady low mood and not really being interested in things… that settled in a while back. I’d say it’s been going on for maybe a year and four months or so. Most days, yeah.
Has this been making it hard for you to function at work or in your daily life?

Yeah… I mean, I’m still getting to work and handling my day-to-day stuff, so I don’t want to overstate it. But it has been harder.

At work I’ve been making some mistakes that I really should’ve caught, just avoidable things. And sometimes a coworker will ask me something simple and I have to ask them to repeat it, like I didn’t take it in the first time. That’s embarrassing.

Outside of work, I’ve kind of stopped going to chess nights or doing photography walks. I tell myself I’m just tired, but honestly I don’t really trust myself to keep up or act normal around people. Does that… is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you been feeling worthless?

Yeah… I guess I have, though I don’t like saying it that way.

It’s more like I keep thinking I’m being a burden, you know? At the clinic, or even with my family. If I make some small mistake—like if a room turnover gets delayed—I’ll go over it in my head like I ruined everyone’s whole day, like I let everybody down. I know that probably sounds a little dramatic, and I’m not trying to be… but that’s where my mind goes.
Have you had thoughts that you’d be better off dead?

Um… not exactly like I want to do something to myself. I haven’t made any kind of plan or anything like that.

But… yeah, I do catch myself thinking sometimes that it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up. Or if I could just disappear for a while and not have to be… here, dealing with everything. I’m sorry, I don’t mean to make that sound alarming. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?
Do these symptoms feel mainly connected to the changes at work?

I think so, yeah… mostly. It really seemed to start after the clinic changed the EMR and the workflow, and my hours got shifted around.

I don’t want to blame everything on work, but that’s when I noticed it becoming a real thing. It’s been… almost two years now, I guess. Which sounds like a long time when I say it out loud.
Do these feelings seem stronger than you’d expect from the changes at work?

I’m not totally sure how to judge that, honestly.

Part of me wants to say it makes sense because work has been stressful, and I don’t want to make it sound bigger than it is. But… maybe it is a little stronger than what other people would have from the same thing? I don’t know. I keep thinking I should be handling it better.

Does that answer what you mean?
Even on days when work isn’t part of the picture, do you still feel down most of the day?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like every single minute is terrible, but even when work isn’t happening that day, a lot of mornings I wake up with this kind of heavy, hollow feeling… like the day’s already gone bad before I’ve even gotten dressed or put on my badge.

I can still get moving, usually, so I don’t know if that counts as “most of the day,” but it’s there more than I’d like to admit.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?

I don’t know… maybe a little, but I haven’t really been tracking it.

I can usually get through what I need to do, so I don’t want to overstate it. Sometimes I’ll reread something or lose my place, but I’m not sure if that’s concentration or just being tired or distracted. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Even when work is going well, do you still feel depressed?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m miserable every second or anything, but even when work is going okay, most mornings I still wake up with that heavy, hollow feeling.

It’s like the day already feels ruined before I’ve even put on my badge, if that makes sense. I can still show up and do what I’m supposed to do, but the feeling is there.
Have there been times when these depression symptoms lasted for at least two weeks and didn’t seem tied to what was happening at work?

Yeah… I think that’s fair to say. I mean, I didn’t really want to call it that at first, because it sounds kind of dramatic, but it wasn’t just a bad week at work or something.

The more steady depression, and not really being interested in much, kind of settled in later… and it’s been there for, I guess, around a year and four months now. Not every second, but long stretches, definitely more than two weeks at a time. Does that make sense?
When you feel down, is that feeling present for most of the day?

Yeah… most days, I think it’s there for a lot of the day. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m completely nonfunctional, because I do get up and go in.

But most mornings I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling, like the day is already kind of ruined before I even put on my badge. Sometimes it eases up a little once I’m moving, but it’s usually there in the background.

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the persistence of feeling down for most of the day, which directly relates to depressed mood.

patient.answer:
Yeah… most days, I think it’s there for a lot of the day. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m completely nonfunctional, because I do get up and go in.

But most mornings I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling, like the day is already kind of ruined before I even put on my badge. Sometimes it eases up a little once I’m moving, but it’s usually there in the background.

inference.note: Symptoms now clearly meet a depressive episode independent of the work stressor: depressed mood most of the day, anhedonia, insomnia, appetite/weight loss, worthlessness, impaired concentration/functioning, and passive death wishes for >2 weeks (about 16 months). This makes F32.A more likely than F43.8.

opening_question.intent: Understand the patient's main reason for seeking psychiatric help today
opening_question.question: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a persistent depressed mood most days for about 1 year and 4 months, markedly reduced interest in previously enjoyed activities, insomnia with early morning awakening, appetite/weight loss, feelings of worthlessness/burdensomeness, passive thoughts of death, and some concentration/work-performance difficulty. Symptoms cause functional impairment and occur even when work stress is not active, making a primary depressive episode more consistent than an adjustment disorder. Trauma-related symptoms were denied, and there is no evidence of mania or weight-gain fear/eating-disorder psychopathology.
